decisions: Blocked on extract_modules.py until one line changes. Plan._residue_reads feeds every non-movable top-level statement to free_names, which wraps it in a function body; this source's 'from __future__ import annotations' makes symtable raise SyntaxError, so the CLI traces back instead of printing a plan. Fix: build kept from statements that are not MOVABLE and not ast.Import or ast.ImportFrom. An import binds names and never reads any, and _unread_imports already handles the import block separately, so nothing else moves. damage.py has no future import, which is why step 1 never hit this. Verified clean with that one change applied.

Blocked on a second extract_modules.py line. module_units._annotation_names treats every string constant inside an annotation as a quoted forward reference, so _Edge's origin: Literal["declared", "inferred"] yields two names bound nowhere and the CLI refuses cast_edge_markers.py. Fix: while walking an annotation, skip the slice of a Subscript whose value is named Literal. Verified clean with that change plus the __future__ one.

Six modules, not the map's four. derive_champion_rule (R6) reads resolved_edges (R4), _kahn_order and detect_aoe_cap (R5) and rank_ability_dps (R7), so the map's remainder of R4, R5 and R7 is a back-edge from champion_rotation_rule. The one honest direction is R4, R5 and the DPS ranking downstream of nothing and upstream of the rule, with the residue holding only resolve_cast_order and build_rotation_receipt, which read derive_champion_rule.

cast_edge_resolution.py is the new module for R4 plus _kahn_order: declarations merged over inferences, and the topological order that admits them. _kahn_order orders _Edge objects, so it belongs with the edges, not with the AoE cap it sat beside.

detect_aoe_cap goes to cast_edge_markers.py, whose docstring widens to say the slot corpus answers both questions. Its only dependency is _slot_corpus, so any other home imports the marker module for one call.

ability_dps_matrix.py splits R6 along the seam the map's own title names. The matrix (_MATRIX_SPECS, _MATRIX_DPS_CACHE, _matrix_dps_rows) plus rank_ability_dps is 87 lines and a leaf; the rule fitted from it is 392. Kept together with rank_ability_dps they render at about 520, over the ceiling, which is what forces the seam rather than taste.
cast_edge_inference.py renders at 477. detect_setup_consume_edges is 462 of that, so about 20 lines of margin: a later edit to that function reopens the finding on a module that holds nothing else.

Residue 280 lines. _validate_override_reasons() is called as a bare module-level statement, which is not a movable unit, so the residue imports it and CAST_ORDER_OVERRIDES back from cast_order_overrides.py and keeps running the check at import.

cast_edge_inference.py is 506 lines and keeps sightline #27's size arm, baselined with this reason: the module is one function, one pass over one champion's rows, and every edge kind reads the same closures (corpora, infos, texts, atexts, add, slot_from_name, has_consume_role). Cutting a kind out means handing that context to it as six parameters, which moves lines and helps no reader.
